pr_title: Ensure created nodes are present in scheduler cache before scheduling
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind flake
/sig scheduling

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

The scheduler integration test usually follows a create-node-and-schedule-pod pattern. However, when the nodes are created successfully, they're not necessarily **immediately** present in the scheduler internal cache (need to wait for the coming of Node events from API server). So an incoming pod may fail the scheduling due to "not having nodes in the cluster", such as #94230 revealed.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #94230

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

⚠️ This PR deprecates `createNodes()` and recommend using `createAndWaitForNodesInCache()` instead. However, callers of `createNode()` are a bit complicated, we cannot simply deprecate it by using a `createAndWaitForNodeInCache()`, e.g.,

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e9294c4ca76145f500b369d6e6e3c3144abf1319/test/integration/scheduler/priorities_test.go#L266-L275

So I'd like to fix `createNode()` in a follow-up by walking through its caller one by one.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
NONE
```

The only exception is [TestUnschedulablePodBecomesSchedulable](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/96062/pull-kubernetes-integration/1323924512827248640), which reveals a flake that when a node is created and then tainted, in rare cases, it's possible the incoming pod can still be scheduled as internal node cache may haven't dealt with the taint event. Once a pod gets scheduled, `waitForPodUnschedulable()` will be always false.

So we may need another PR fixing this, and as the description section stated, along with fixing other `createNode()` leftovers., in a case-by-case manner.

issue_context.title: [Flaky Test] [sig-scheduling] k8s.io/kubernetes/test/integration/scheduler.TestPostFilterPlugin
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting reports about flaky tests or jobs (pass or fail with no underlying change in code) in Kubernetes CI -->

**Which jobs are flaking**:

`integration-master (ci-kubernetes-integration-master )`

**Which test(s) are flaking**:

`k8s.io/kubernetes/test/integration/scheduler.TestPostFilterPlugin`

**Testgrid link**:

https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-release-master-blocking#integration-master

**Reason for failure**:

```
framework_test.go:666: Expected the filter plugin to be called at least 2 times, but got 0.
    framework_test.go:669: Expected the postfilter plugin to be called at least 1 times, but got 0.
```

**Anything else we need to know**:

/cc @kubernetes/ci-signal @kubernetes/sig-scheduling-bugs @Huang-Wei 
/sig scheduling
/milestone v1.19
/priority critical-urgent

xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93485
comments:
@hasheddan thanks for raising this up. I think this is not a releasing blocking flake, but still a flake that can happen with rare chances.

The logs says:

```
12245 I0825 15:14:39.147789  119315 factory.go:443] "Unable to schedule pod; no nodes are registered to the cluster; waiting" pod="postfilter2-0e1f1596-ea0      0-448f-807b-035f107417ef/test-pod"
```

This implies the integration test env is not prepared well - the (virtual) nodes are not ready - and then we proceed with the testing logic. A simple fix will be to add logic to ensure all (virtual) nodes to become available, and the logic would be good to be applied as a common pattern to all similar test cases.
@Huang-Wei Will you get a chance to look at this for the 1.20 release or would you like to get some help with this?
Ready to work on this, got another DP [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/82222#issuecomment-719699190).

I added the code the following and tried to reproduce this problem in my local environment.
```
// Filter is a test function that returns an error or nil, depending on the
// value of "failFilter".
func (fp *FilterPlugin) Filter(ctx context.Context, state *framework.CycleState, pod *v1.Pod, nodeInfo *framework.NodeInfo) *framework.Status {
        fp.numFilterCalled++

        fmt.Printf("Pod=%v Node=%v called=%v\n", pod.Name, (*nodeInfo).Node().Name, fp.numFilterCalled)  <=== *
```
As a result, the following message was output.
So, "fp.numFilterCalled++" is not thread safe and seems to be causing this issue.
```
Pod=test-pod Node=test-node-0 called=1
Pod=test-pod Node=test-node-1 called=2  <=== *
Pod=test-pod Node=test-node-2 called=2  <=== *
```

I think it should be changed to such as atomic.AddInt32, what do you think about it?

@s-ito-ts yes, the latest code has switched to atomic.AddInt32():

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6a3fd8f3d71e756f4231b610fb1d404abb100119/test/integration/scheduler/framework_test.go#L232-L233

@Huang-Wei Thank you for your reply.
I seem to have seen the old code.

Please let me ask one more thing.
It seems that there are still some similar codes in the latest code.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6a3fd8f3d71e756f4231b610fb1d404abb100119/test/integration/scheduler/framework_test.go#L252-L253

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6a3fd8f3d71e756f4231b610fb1d404abb100119/test/integration/scheduler/framework_test.go#L404-L405

I think these codes should also be switched to atomic.AddInt32().
Will it help you if I change these codes?
@s-ito-ts Reserve and PostFilter plugins are executed sequentially, so it's fine to leave the counter as is.

@Huang-Wei I understand.
Thank you for explaining in detail.

review_comments: restore this line so that the comment is not associated to the function below.
nit: revert. The extra context doesn't hurt. Same for other Fatal calls.
I deliberately let `createAndWaitForNodesInCache()` return the error with context - failed to create nodes, or fail to obtain nodes in cache. So let's just use `err` in the caller side.
Also say here to not use outside of tests.
